summary: Completed testing iteration 3 - Auth loading race condition successfully fixed! Both admin and brand authentication flows now work perfectly. Users can login and access protected routes (/admin, /brand/dashboard) without being redirected to login. However, found backend issue with product creation (MongoDB ObjectId serialization error).

critical_bugs.issue: 500 Internal Server Error when creating new products - MongoDB ObjectId serialization issue
critical_bugs.impact: Prevents brands from adding new products to their catalog
critical_bugs.error_details: ValueError: [TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable"), TypeError('vars() argument must have __dict__ attribute')]

ui_bugs.issue: Dialog remains open after failed product submission due to backend 500 error
ui_bugs.impact: User doesn't get clear feedback that product creation failed

passed_tests: Admin login with admin@ukstreetwear.com / Admin123! works correctly
Admin can access /admin dashboard without redirect to login
Admin dashboard displays stats panel with Users: 7, Brands: 4, Products: 3
Admin dashboard shows brand applications and brand management sections
Demo brand login with demo@threadandbone.uk / Demo123! works correctly
Demo brand can access /brand/dashboard without redirect to login
Brand dashboard shows 'Thread & Bone' brand name correctly
Brand dashboard displays 3 products count correctly
Brand dashboard shows existing products: Smithfield Hoodie (£85.00), Workshop Cargos (£68.00), BrickLane Tee (£35.00)
Brand status shows 'Boosted' and 'Brand of Week' badges correctly
Add Product button is clickable and opens dialog
Add Product dialog form fields can be filled (name, description, price, stock, category, sizes, images)
Auth loading race condition completely resolved - no more redirects to login for authenticated users
action_item_for_main_agent: Fix backend MongoDB ObjectId serialization issue in product creation endpoint (/api/products POST). The error occurs when trying to return the created product object containing ObjectId fields. Need to ensure ObjectId fields are properly converted to strings before JSON serialization.
